cluster_summary: Multiple vulnerabilities arise from failing to enforce upper bounds on user-controlled size parameters (query limits, object indices) or from neglecting to check field metadata (types like Password, Email) before exposing data through queries, exports, REST APIs, and diffs. These omissions lead to resource exhaustion or unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.
guideline_text: Trace untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata into deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation. Report code paths where allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization.

mechanism.missing_guard: allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization
mechanism.name: untrusted deserialization with attacker-controlled type graph
mechanism.sink_shape: deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation
mechanism.source_shape: untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add type-based checks at each output point: skip or mask fields of sensitive types, obfuscate emails according to configuration, and ensure class metadata is preserved in diffs.
sub_patterns.name: Sensitive data exposure via missing field-type checks in query building and serialization
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code that builds database queries, generates XML exports, computes diffs, or returns REST responses does not inspect field metadata (e.g., Password, Email types) before including or exposing property values, allowing unprivileged users to read confidential data.
